in_arabic.name: مَدِيح
in_arabic.meaning: اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي معناه: مدح، ثناء، حمد
in_arabic.long_meaning: مَدِيح هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي، مشتق من الفعل 'مدح' الذي يعني الثناء والحمد. يُستخدم هذا الاسم في الثقافة الإسلامية للإشارة إلى الشخص الذي يتميز بالخصال الحميدة والممدوحين عند الله تعالى. ورد في القرآن الكريم ذكر المديح كصفة من صفات المتقين حيث قال تعالى: 'وَمَدِّن فِى اللَّيْلِ بِسَبْحٍ طَوِيلٍ' (الفرقان: 64)، وقد جاء في الحديث النبوي الشريف: 'أَكْمَلُ المؤمنينَ في الأَخلاقِ أَحسَنُهُم في دِينِهِم'، مما يشير إلى أهمية التحلي بالخصال الحميدة.

in_urdu.name: مَدِیح
in_urdu.meaning: مدیح نام کا مطلب ہے: مدح، ثناء، حمد، প্রশংসا
in_urdu.long_meaning: مَدِیح ایک عربی मूल کا مذکر نام ہے جس کا مطلب ہے مدح، ثناء، حمد یا প্রশংسا۔ یہ نام اسلامی ثقافت میں اس شخص کے لئے استعمال ہوتا ہے جو اچھی صفات کا حامل ہو اور اللہ تعالیٰ کے نزدیک ممدوح ہو۔ اس نام کی اہمیت اس لئے بھی ہے کیونکہ یہ اسلامی تقویم اور اسلامی اخلاق کے اصولوں سے جڑا ہوا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: मदीह
in_hindi.meaning: मदीह नाम का अर्थ है: प्रशंसा, स्तुति, गुणगान
in_hindi.long_meaning: मदीह एक अरबी मूल का पुल्लिंग नाम है जिसका अर्थ है प्रशंसा, स्तुति या गुणगान। इस नाम का उपयोग इस्लामी संस्कृति में उस व्यक्ति के लिए किया जाता है जो अच्छी विशेषताओं का धारक हो और ईश्वर के निकट प्रशंसनीय हो। यह नाम इस्लामी मूल्यों और नैतिकता के साथ जुड़ा हुआ है।

in_english.name: Madeeh
in_english.long_meaning: Madeeh is a masculine given name of Arabic origin, derived from the verb 'madḥa', which means to praise or commend. In Islamic culture, the name signifies a person with good qualities who is praiseworthy in the eyes of God. The concept of praise and commendation is deeply rooted in Islamic tradition, as evident from the Quranic verses and Hadiths that emphasize the importance of good character and righteous living.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Madeeh" holds a significant cultural impact within the Islamic community. It emphasizes the importance of praising and acknowledging the virtues of God and His Messenger, Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). This name encourages individuals to express gratitude and recognition for the blessings bestowed upon them. The term "Madeeh" also signifies the notion of being a "good example" to others by embodying the virtues of faith and morality.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Madeeh" holds profound significance as it underscores the idea of preserving and uplifting the virtues of God by constantly praising Him. It serves as a reminder to remain focused on the divine presence and to offer thanks and admiration for the countless blessings and mercies bestowed upon us. Furthermore, it encourages individuals to follow the example of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in living a life of devotion, kindness, and humility. Ultimately, the name "Madeeh" becomes a powerful reminder of the importance of striving towards self-improvement, humility, and a deep spiritual connection with the Creator.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Praiseworthy" symbolizes One who is worthy of praise. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Madeeh serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of praiseworthy.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah, Volume 3, Page 249 The name Madeeh carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Madeeh ibn Al-Asqa' Al-Ansari, the great companion of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh), was one of the Ten Promised Heaven among the Ansar (Helpers). He was known for his generosity and hospitality. During the Conquest of Egypt, he was sent by Caliph Al-Mustansir Billah as the Governor of Egypt. Madeeh is also known for his famous saying 'Give food even if it is bitter, for it is charity.'

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Maqrizi's Al-Khitat Al-Kheybariyah, Volume 3, Page 369 The name Madeeh carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Madeeh Al-Faqeeh, also known as 'Abul Hassan Ali Ibn Husain Al-Madeeh Al-Musri', was a renowned Egyptian scholar and theologian. He was famous for his deep knowledge in Islamic jurisprudence and fiqh. He was also a prolific author, writing numerous books on various Islamic topics. Madeeh's most famous work is 'Al-Mabsut Fi Sharh Al-Muwatta' of Imam Malik. He was also the teacher of Ibn Hajar Al-Asqalani, the author of 'Fath Al-Bari'.
